newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat settles at six-month highs.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat settles at six-month highs.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures climbed higher on spillover input from other U.S. wheat markets and settled at six-month highs, traders said.

Nearby May rose 3-1/2 cents per bushel to settle at $4.12-3/4. That marked the contract's highest close since September 13, when it settled at $4.15. July and September spring wheat contracts also closed at six-month highs.

"I've been talking with various people all day and nobody seems to know why we're so strong. I think we're trying to stay competitive with Chicago, but also people are still talking about planting delays," a trader said.

The flood watch continued Wednesday in the key spring wheat growing region of the Red River Valley. The National Weather Service anticipates severe floods on the river, which could prompt serious planting delays and even a decline in spring wheat acreage.
Traders also said spring wheat was attracting speculative interest amid feelings that spring wheat acreage may be lower as farmers shift acres to more attractively priced oilseeds.
Overall, spring wheat settled three to five cents higher, with Sept up 3-3/4 cents at $4.00-3/4.
MGE barley futures did not trade.
